rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadmin lets a verb take another verb’s sense and preposition: “سمع” with “لـ” means respond (“استجاب”), not merely hear; not every hearing entails response.
rows.anchor: التضمين في النحو هو إشراب لفظ معنى لفظ آخر فيأخذ حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using نصر with من in 21:77 imports نجّى’s sense of deliverance: God both rescued the prophet and defeated the people; من in 29:24 denotes rescue alone, since fire cannot be defeated.
rows.anchor: عدّى الفعل نصر بما يتعدّى به فعل نجّى أي بحرف (من) وذلك للدلالة على أن المعنى المطلوب

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says speakers advance what matters most to them and occupies their greatest concern.
rows.anchor: يقول سيبويه في التقديم والتأخير: يقدمون الذي هو أهمّ لهم وهم أعنى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the surrounding Al Imran passage concerns Mary, not Zechariah or the mihrab, the wording foregrounds her in “عليها زكريا.”
rows.anchor: الكلام في الآية في سورة آل عمران والآيات التي سبقتها في مريم عليها السلام وليس في زكريا ولا في المحراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order differs with the verse endings: al-Isra ends with God’s attributes, so “شهيداً” comes first; al-Ankabut ends by describing human loss, so “بيني وبينكم” comes first.
rows.anchor: في آية سورة الإسراء ختم تعالى الآية بذكر صفاته (خبيراً بصيرا) لذا اقتضى أن يُقدّم صفته (شهيداً)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes varying placements of “above you/them” and “the Mount” in accounts of the covenant with the Children of Israel as another example of contextual ordering.
rows.anchor: وقال في سورة الأعراف (وَإِذ نَتَقْنَا الْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “مالك الملك” combines ownership and sovereign rule: Pharaoh claimed Egypt’s rule, not its ownership, while God owns and governs the kingdom; the title gathers both powers.
rows.anchor: هو مالك من التملّك ومن المِلك (الملكية) والمُلك من الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “نباتاً حسناً” credits Mary’s responsive nature and willing growth alongside God’s nurturing; “إنباتاً” would present the process solely as God’s act and omit her merit.
rows.anchor: أن لها فضل في هذا ولو قال تعالى إنباتاً لكان كله عملية لله وحده وليس لمريم أي فضل

words: عَمَّآ أَجْرَمْنَا وَلَا نُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this invitation context, assigning possible wrongdoing to the believers while neutrally saying opponents’ “deeds” is scrupulously fair, meant to win their hearts and keep the door of preaching open.
rows.anchor: هذا من باب الإنصاف في الكلام حتى يستميلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without mentioning any possession, “غني حميد” means God needs neither thanks nor disbelief; after stating His ownership of heaven and earth, “هو الغني الحميد” marks His unmatched wealth and praise.
rows.anchor: فعندما ذكر له ملك السموات والأرض المتسع، فمن أغنى منه؟ فقال (هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman’s wisdom is practical as well as verbal: personally tending and advising his son models parents’ duty to guide children instead of leaving them to bad teachers or the streets.
rows.anchor: حكمة لقمان ليست فيما ذكره من أحاديث وأقوال وما قاله لابنه من الوصية، وإنما أيضا في العمل الذي فعله

words: فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited “لا جناح” passages concern rights and family matters, while the Safa and Marwa example concerns worship.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات كلها في الحقوق وفي شؤون الأسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s family wording reflects the Prophet’s one maternal uncle and multiple maternal aunts; the source names Faria bint Wahb and Fakhta among the aunts.
rows.anchor: له خالات وله خال واحد. يذكرون من خالاته فريعة بنت وهب ويذكر خالة اسمها فاختة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though he had many paternal uncles and aunts, most cousins were married; Abu Talib had one daughter, while daughters of foster-brothers Abbas and Hamza were ineligible because nursing made them siblings.
rows.anchor: فيكون له عم واحد فقط له ابنة والباقي متزوجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because inspiration can mean ordinary ilham to Moses’ mother, the bee, or humans and jinn, “علمه شديد القوى” identifies Gabriel as the revealer who taught Muhammad; God remains the ultimate teacher.
rows.anchor: فأراد سبحانه أن يقطع أي فكرة فقال (علّمه شديد القوى) بمعنى أنه ليس إلهاماً ولكنه وحي علّمه إياه شديد القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form “علّمه” conveys sustained, repeated teaching, unlike “أعلّمه.”
rows.anchor: وفعل علّمه تفيد المداومة والتكثير على خلاف أُعلّمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two attributes signify strength and knowledge, sound judgment, and precision needed for the ascent and for Gabriel to protect the Prophet and preserve revelation; crossing the heavens also requires “سلطان.”
rows.anchor: هاتان الصفتان فيهما إشارة أن الخروج إلى أقطار السموات يحتاج إلى أمرين هما القوة والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma’idah discusses who has authority to declare things lawful or forbidden and rejects any authority besides God, who rules as He wills.
rows.anchor: والكلام في المائدة أيضاً على التحليل والتجريم ومن بيده ذلك، ورفض أية جهة تحلل وتحرم من غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma’idah places “لغير الله” before “به” to foreground rejection of shirk; its prohibition of deliberate failure to name God and command to name Him over slaughter make this order apt.
rows.anchor: ولذا قدمه في البطلان فقال (وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Baqarah, the passage focuses on provision and food, so it advances “به” before “لغير الله,” keeping the slaughtered food in focus.
rows.anchor: فلما كان المقام مقام الرزق والطعام بأكل الطيبات قدم (به) والضمير يعود على ما يذبح وهو طعام مناسبة للمقام والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasra is more intense than ordinary regret: a consuming remorse that leaves someone unable to act or recover what was lost. Cain is described as regretful; other verses picture regret as useless and irretrievable.
rows.anchor: الحسرة هي أشد الندم حتى ينقطع الإنسان من أن يفعل شيئاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm is hot water, though also used for cold water as a lexical opposite; yaḥmūm is intensely black smoke.
rows.anchor: من حمّ والحمّى. والحميم يأتي من الشيء وضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “سولت” means the self embellished and eased an act; “طوعت” is stronger, requiring effort to train the self. Cain had to overcome resistance to killing his brother, unlike the easier acts of the Samiri and Joseph’s brothers; the Quran’s terms are not interchangeable.
rows.anchor: فيها جهد ومبالغة في التطويع حتى تروضه وتذلله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “آلاف” is a broken plural of paucity, conventionally three to ten; “ألوف” is a plural of multitude for numbers above ten, explaining the Quran’s forms.
rows.anchor: آلآف من أوزان القِلّة، جمع قلة. (أفعال) من أوزان القِلّة
